triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '14. `bf16_trunc_pack_v*` is not dtype-aware — silently wrecks fp16 output' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 14. `bf16_trunc_pack_v*` is not dtype-aware — silently wrecks fp16 output

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 14. `bf16_trunc_pack_v*` is not dtype-aware — silently wrecks fp16 output

payload.attempted: To pack 4/8 f32 accumulator values into v4bf16 / v8bf16 for the P softmax output (and v13's O writeback), it's tempting to AND off the low 16 bits of each f32 and OR-shift them into i32 dwords. bf16 IS the upper 16 bits of f32 (same exponent layout, same bias, just truncated mantissa) so this is ~2 fewer ops per element than `arith.TruncFOp`. Helper named `bf16_trunc_pack_v4` made this explicit.
payload.lesson: 16-bit float pack helpers must branch on dtype:

established_fact.mechanism: fp16 (IEEE binary16) has a 5-bit exponent and bias 15. f32 has 8-bit exponent and bias 127. The high 16 bits of f32 are NOT a valid fp16 representation — different exponent field width, different bias, completely different bit layout. Bitwise truncation produces an fp16 with whatever random bits happened to be in the top half of the f32 → essentially random data.

payload.observed: fp16 outputs are garbage (max abs err ≫ noise — the kernel "runs" but values are arbitrary). Bug went unnoticed because the entire optimization journey (v0 → v14, all perf benches, all correctness checks) was run on bf16 only. fp16 build only flagged when a downstream user exercised it.
payload.root_cause: fp16 (IEEE binary16) has a 5-bit exponent and bias 15. f32 has 8-bit exponent and bias 127. The high 16 bits of f32 are NOT a valid fp16 representation — different exponent field width, different bias, completely different bit layout. Bitwise truncation produces an fp16 with whatever random bits happened to be in the top half of the f32 → essentially random data.
